title: Canonical base-change map for a right adjoint
statement: Given a cartesian square of quasi-compact and quasi-separated schemes X'=X\times_Y Y' with g_X:X'\to X, f':X'\to Y', f:X\to Y, and g:Y'\to Y [def-pc-fibre-product], let a and a' be right adjoints to Rf_* and Rf'_* on quasi-coherent derived categories [def-pc-derived-category, def-pc-derived-direct-image, lem-pc-qcqs-derived-direct-image-right-adjoint], and let \beta: Lg^*Rf_*\to Rf'_*Lg_X^* be the canonical base-change transformation on D_{\mathrm{QCoh}}(X) (the adjoint, under Lg^*\dashv Rg_*, of Rf_*(\eta):Rf_*\to Rf_*Rg_{X,*}Lg_X^*=Rg_*Rf'_*Lg_X^*, with \eta the unit of Lg_X^*\dashv Rg_{X,*} [def-pc-derived-pullback]). Assume \beta is an isomorphism. Let \theta: Rg_{X,*}a'\to aRg_* be the conjugate of \beta, i.e. the transformation between the right adjoints of Rf'_*Lg_X^* and Lg^*Rf_* corresponding to \beta; \theta is an isomorphism because \beta is. For K in D_{\mathrm{QCoh}}(Y), the canonical right-adjoint base-change morphism Lg_X^*a(K)\to a'(Lg^*K) is the composite $$Lg_X^*a(K)\xrightarrow{Lg_X^*a(\eta'_K)}Lg_X^*aRg_*Lg^*K\xrightarrow{Lg_X^*(\theta_{Lg^*K})^{-1}}Lg_X^*Rg_{X,*}a'(Lg^*K)\xrightarrow{\epsilon}a'(Lg^*K),$$ where \eta':\mathrm{id}\to Rg_*Lg^* is the unit of Lg^*\dashv Rg_* and \epsilon is the counit of Lg_X^*\dashv Rg_{X,*} [def-pc-derived-pullback] (Stacks, duality.tex, equation-base-change-map).

proof.text: Lift schemeDerivedBaseChangeMap to a natural transformation beta: Rf ⋙ Lg -> LgX ⋙ Rf'. Prove naturality by transposing the counit composite: naturality of the composition comparisons, transport along the pullback equation, and counit naturality give the result. This uses the canonical ordinary base-change construction, not new choices of its data.

proof.text: Apply Mathlib CategoryTheory.mateEquiv adjf adjf' to inverse beta and evaluate at K. This is the required map LgX(a(K)) -> a'(Lg(K)). The iterated_mateEquiv_conjugateEquiv identity, together with conjugateEquiv_comm and the inverse mate component formula, identifies it with the stated unit/inverse-conjugate/counit composite for any auxiliary pullback adjunctions. The direct formula needs only adjf, adjf' and beta and eliminates both auxiliary choices. The already proved private secondMate_formula in QCohInverseBaseChangeMate gives this generic calculation; that downstream module is not imported (which would create a cycle).
